oil.summary: Crude markets pushed higher on Tuesday as a cascade of geopolitical shocks kept the risk premium firmly bid. Brent crossed $91/bbl (+0.48%) and WTI held $84.64 (+0.19%) after an unidentified projectile struck a vessel transiting the Strait of Hormuz and Iran reiterated its blockade will remain in place until U.S. conditions are met. Houthis claimed a third strike on Saudi Aramco's Jazan refinery in two weeks, amplifying supply-disruption anxiety. Gulf-to-China VLCC rates surged to $510,000/day, reflecting the freight risk premium. The sharp divergence in refined products—RBOB gasoline collapsing 8.27% on the session versus heating oil off only 3.0%—is notable and warrants monitoring for structural demand signals. U.S. shale majors are reportedly trimming capex rather than chasing volumes, limiting any near-term supply response to elevated prices.
drivers: Hormuz closure threat sustained after vessel strike and Iran's conditional blockade statement keep geopolitical risk premium elevated in Brent
Third Houthi attack on Jazan refinery in two weeks tightens Middle East refining capacity and supports distillate margins
RBOB gasoline -8.27% intraday divergence from crude signals potential demand softness or domestic supply normalisation worth tracking

gas.summary: Natural gas markets traded with a split personality on Tuesday. Henry Hub edged up 1.34% to $2.727/MMBtu but remains under pressure on the month (-4.69%), reflecting ample domestic supply. European TTF, by contrast, gained 1.33% to €62.58/MWh and is up 6.55% on the week, consistent with the broader Hormuz-driven LNG supply anxiety. Pakistan's power generation costs jumped 38% year-on-year in July after the country paid the highest spot LNG prices in four years, an early indication of how Gulf supply disruptions translate into Asian and emerging-market energy costs. Headline flow for Henry Hub is thin today; the U.S.-domestic gas narrative is largely being driven by macro and storage dynamics not captured in today's feed.
drivers: TTF +6.55% on the week as Hormuz tensions tighten European LNG re-supply expectations
Pakistan spot LNG costs hit four-year highs in July, illustrating emerging-market demand destruction risk from supply disruptions
Henry Hub -4.69% on the month reflects resilient domestic U.S. production offsetting geopolitical premium

power.summary: EU carbon allowances (EUA) edged up 0.43% to $78.15, extending a steady month-long grind higher (+3.85%), supported by TTF's upward move and the broader energy cost pass-through dynamic. Iran's repeated affirmation that the Strait of Hormuz will remain closed until U.S. interim deal conditions are met continues to anchor elevated gas prices, which in turn supports carbon costs as gas-fired generation competes with coal across European dispatch stacks. Ukraine's deep-strike operations against Russian energy infrastructure add a secondary upside tail risk to TTF and, by extension, EUAs. Pakistan's 38% power cost surge underlines how LNG-price spikes ripple through power markets in gas-dependent economies. Dedicated power-sector news flow is light today beyond these cross-commodity linkages.
drivers: EUA +3.85% on the month as elevated TTF raises gas-to-coal switching thresholds and supports carbon demand
Hormuz closure and Ukraine strikes on Russian energy infrastructure sustain upside risk to European gas and power prices
Pakistan power cost data (+38% YoY) highlights LNG-price transmission into power markets, a pattern relevant to any European gas demand resurgence
